# REST API reference

<!-- Generated by docs/tools/openapi_to_markdown.py from /v3/api-docs. Do not edit by hand; edit the controllers or docs/api-reference-notes.md. -->

PARI backend API version 0.0.1. Parking space rental portal. Authenticate with a JWT from POST /api/auth/login (Authorize button). Payments use a mock gateway.

51 operations in 13 controllers. Every operation needs `Authorization: Bearer <JWT>` unless the table says *public*. Errors, roles and business rules are in [Notes](#notes-on-the-api).

**Bookable spaces in one listing (PARI-65, ADR 0006, part 1 of 3).** A listing is one or more numbered spaces ("units") at the same address. The shared data (address, photos, description, prices, gate PIN, access instructions) stays on the listing; a unit has an `id` (the identifier) and a `label` (display only, `#1`, `#2`, ..., 1 to 20 characters, unique among the live spaces of the listing, case-insensitive). Every listing, also the existing ones, has at least `#1`. `POST /api/spots` accepts `unitCount` (1 to `max_units_per_spot`, default 1) and creates `#1` to `#n`. `GET /api/spots/{id}/units` lists the live spaces with their ids (also `SpotView.units`); `POST` adds one (without a label the next free `#n`), `PUT` renames, `DELETE` removes one; each returns the live spaces afterwards. Errors: `409 SPOT_UNIT_LABEL_TAKEN`, `409 SPOT_UNIT_LIMIT` (the limit is the placeholder setting `max_units_per_spot` = 50), `409 SPOT_UNIT_LAST` (the last space cannot be removed, archive the listing instead), `409 SPOT_UNIT_HAS_RESERVATIONS` (a reservation still holds the space, `details.label`), `400` for a bad label or a bad `unitCount`, `404` for an unknown space, `403` for anyone but the owner or an ADMIN. A removed space is kept, so old reservations keep their unit and the label they had. The database now guarantees no overlap per space (`reservations_no_overlap` is keyed on `unit_id`). **Booking (part 2 of 3).** `POST /api/reservations` takes an optional `unitId`. Without it the first live space that is free for the whole range (including the unpaid buffer) is assigned; the listing row is locked while booking, so concurrent requests are decided one at a time, and the exclusion constraint stays the final guard. Different spaces of one listing can be booked for the same time, one space cannot. `ReservationView` returns `unitId` and `unitLabel`. Map search returns a listing while at least one space is free and reports `freeUnits`. **Not available yet** (the third pull request): per-space blocks and the parent-wide closure, the owner calendar, occupancy per space, and the label in notifications, support views and receipts. Until then a blocked period still applies to the whole listing.

**Blocks, calendar, occupancy and labels (part 3 of 3).** A blocked period (`POST .../blocked-periods` or `.../calendar/blocks`) takes an optional `unitId`: with it only that space is closed, without it every space is (a listing-wide closure). A space block is refused (409 `PERIOD_HAS_RESERVATIONS`) only when that space has a reservation in the period, a listing-wide closure when any space has. Booking skips blocked spaces; a named space that is blocked gives 409 `SPOT_NOT_AVAILABLE`. Weekly rules and extra open periods stay at listing level. Search counts only the spaces that are neither booked nor blocked. `GET /api/spots/{id}/booked-slots` names the space of each reservation and block (`unitId`, `unitLabel`) and accepts `?unitId=`. **Occupancy** (check-in and check-out) now belongs to the space: `SpotView.occupancy` is `OCCUPIED` only when every live space is, and `occupiedUnits` / `totalUnits` give the counts. The SSE `occupancy` event adds `unitId`, `unitLabel`, `occupiedUnits` and `totalUnits` to the listing-level `occupancy`. **Labels:** `unitId` and `unitLabel` are in `ReservationView`, the support reservation context (`SupportReservationView`) and the booked-slots calendar; notifications carry `unitLabel` in their payload, and their text names the space (`"Garage" (#2)`) for a listing with more than one space. There is no separate receipt document: the reservation (`ReservationView`) with its price breakdown is the receipt, and it carries the label that was valid when it was booked.

**Photo management (PARI-64).** `GET /api/spots/{id}/photos` lists the photos with their stable ids, `position` (0 is the cover) and public `url`; it follows the visibility of the space (an inactive space is visible to its owner only). The same photos are in `SpotView.photos` (`id`, `storageKey`, `position`); `photoKeys` is kept for existing clients. `PUT .../photos/cover` uploads a new image, makes it the cover and removes the previous cover's record and file; the other photos keep their order. On a space without photos it simply adds one. `PUT .../photos/order` takes the ids of every photo of the space exactly once, in the wanted order (the first becomes the cover); a missing, repeated or unknown id gives `400` and changes nothing. Deleting a photo renumbers the rest. Add, replace, reorder and delete are for the owner or an `ADMIN` (`403` for anyone else, `404` for an unknown or archived space, and no file is written for a refused upload). A file whose database update fails is removed again, so a replaced or deleted photo leaves no record and no file behind. Not done: reordering by moving a single photo, and cleaning up files that were stored through `/api/media/upload` and never attached.

| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | path | string (uuid) | yes |  |
| `photoId` | path | string (uuid) | yes |  |

## notification-controller

| Method | Path | Access | Request | Response |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| PATCH | `/api/notifications/tickets/{ticketId}/read` | token |  | `200` `{"updated": n}` |
| PATCH | `/api/notifications/{id}/read` | token |  | `200` NotificationView |
| GET | `/api/notifications` | token |  | `200` array of NotificationView |

**Support-reply notifications (PARI-86).** When a SUPPORT or ADMIN user posts a public reply on a ticket, the ticket's reporter gets one `TICKET_REPLY` notification (channel IN_APP) with `ticketId`, `messageId` and `reservationId` set. Internal notes create none, and neither does a reply by the reporter. The notification is stored, so `GET /api/notifications` returns the same read state after a reload or a new login. A repeated delivery of the same reply never creates a second one. `PATCH /api/notifications/{id}/read` reads one notification; `PATCH /api/notifications/tickets/{ticketId}/read` reads every unread notification of the caller about that ticket and returns how many changed (0 for an unknown ticket or when nothing is unread); it never touches other tickets or other users. Tickets opened by the system have no reporter, so a reply there creates no notification.

## Notes on the API

These notes are written by hand and appended to the generated tables above. They describe what the OpenAPI document cannot: who may call what, how errors look, and the conventions every endpoint follows. They describe the code on `main`; planned behaviour is marked *planned*.

### Authentication

- `POST /api/auth/login` returns `{ token, tokenType, expiresIn, user }` (`expiresIn` in seconds; a blocked account gets `403`). The token is a JWT signed with HS256 (`PARI_JWT_SECRET`), valid 24 h (`pari.security.jwt.ttl`). Its claims are `sub` (the user id) and `roles` (for example `["OWNER"]`). Send it as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.
- There are no refresh tokens and a token cannot be revoked: after a password change (`POST /api/auth/change-password`) or logout, tokens issued earlier stay valid until they expire. *Planned*: refresh tokens (the `auth_tokens` table exists).
- Public endpoints (no token): register, login, `GET /api/spots` (search), `GET /api/spots/{id}`, `GET /api/spots/{id}/reviews`, `GET /api/spots/{id}/availability-rules`, `GET /api/spots/events` (SSE), `POST /api/reservations/quote`, `GET /media/**`, Swagger UI and `/v3/api-docs`. `GET /api/spots/mine` needs a token.
- `X-User-Id: <uuid>` is accepted instead of a token **only** when `pari.security.jwt.dev-header-auth=true` (profile `local` and the tests). It is off by default and must never be on in production. A frontend that sends both headers is fine: the header is ignored when a token is present.
- A missing or invalid token gives `401 UNAUTHENTICATED`.

### Who may do what

The user id always comes from the token, never from the request body. Rules are enforced in the services.

| Action | Rule | Failure |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Register | every account gets `DRIVER` and `OWNER`; the optional `role` (`DRIVER` or `OWNER`, else `400`) only sets the starting panel; e-mail and phone number unique | `400`, `409 EMAIL_ALREADY_REGISTERED`, `409 PHONE_ALREADY_REGISTERED` |
| Create a space (`POST /api/spots`) | `OWNER` role, account not blocked, `ownershipDeclared = true` (F09), price > 0 | `403`, `400` |
| Edit, archive, photos, calendar of a space | the owner of the space, or an `ADMIN` | `404` unknown space, `403` someone else's |
| See a space | public while `ACTIVE`; any other status only for its owner | `404` |
| Book (`POST /api/reservations`) | `DRIVER` role, not the owner of the space, space bookable, owner offers the time, slot free, vehicle belongs to the driver and has no other reservation (any space, statuses `PENDING_PAYMENT`, `PENDING_APPROVAL`, `CONFIRMED`, `IN_PROGRESS`; intervals are half-open, so back-to-back is fine) | `403`, `409 SPOT_NOT_BOOKABLE`, `409 SPOT_NOT_AVAILABLE`, `409 SPOT_ALREADY_RESERVED`, `409 VEHICLE_TIME_CONFLICT` (`details`: `conflictingReservationId`, `conflictingStart`, `conflictingEnd`), `402 PAYMENT_FAILED` |
| Accept or reject a request | the owner of the space; status must be `PENDING_APPROVAL` | `403`, `409 INVALID_STATE` |
| Cancel | the driver or the owner of the reservation; only before check-in | `409 INVALID_STATE` |
| Check in | the driver of the reservation, with the PIN or the QR token, from 5 minutes before the start until the reserved end; the booked interval and amount do not change | `403 Invalid access code`, `409 CHECK_IN_TOO_EARLY` (body has `details.availableAt`, the moment check-in opens), `409 INVALID_STATE` |
| Check out, active session | the driver of the reservation | `409 INVALID_STATE`, `404` |
| Review a space | the driver of a `COMPLETED` reservation, once | `409 RESERVATION_NOT_COMPLETED`, `409 ALREADY_REVIEWED` |
| Owner analytics, payout balance, withdraw, history | `OWNER` role | `403` |
| Withdraw | amount (at most two decimals) not above the available balance | `409 INSUFFICIENT_BALANCE`, `402 PAYMENT_FAILED` |
| Premium (`POST /api/subscriptions/premium`) | `OWNER` role, no active plan | `409 ALREADY_PREMIUM`, `402 PAYMENT_FAILED` |
| Vehicles | own vehicles only; unique plate per user; not deletable while used | `409 VEHICLE_ALREADY_EXISTS`, `VEHICLE_IN_ACTIVE_RESERVATION`, `VEHICLE_HAS_RESERVATION_HISTORY` |
| Block a period in the calendar | the owner; refused while a reservation holds a slot in it | `409 PERIOD_HAS_RESERVATIONS` |
| Archive a space | the owner; refused while a reservation holds a slot | `409 SPOT_HAS_ACTIVE_RESERVATIONS` |

### Gate PIN and access details

Three different things are easy to mix up:

| What | Where | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `ownerGatePin` | on the space (`POST`/`PUT /api/spots`, `GET /api/spots/{id}`, `GET /api/spots/mine`) | The code of the owner's gate or barrier. Stored encrypted. Returned to the owner of the space only; never in search results, never to another user. A `PUT` replaces it as a whole: a missing, null or blank value clears it. |
| `ownerGatePinSnapshot`, `accessInstructionsSnapshot` | on the reservation (`ReservationView`) | What the owner had configured at the moment the reservation was confirmed (paid, or accepted by the owner). Fixed from then on: editing or clearing the space later changes future reservations only. The driver and the owner of the reservation see them, also after check-out or cancellation. They are null for reservations confirmed before this existed and for spaces that had no PIN. |
| `pinCode`, `qrToken` | on the reservation | The generated check-in credential. Only the driver sees it, only while the reservation is confirmed or running. Check-in is validated against these two, never against the gate PIN. |

The legacy `PS_META` marker that the frontend wrote into the space description is not read by the backend. The description is stored and returned as it is; the frontend should move the PIN to `ownerGatePin` and stop writing the marker.

### Support tickets and moderation

Drivers and owners use `/api/tickets` (open a ticket for a reservation, list, read, write a message). The support page uses `/api/support/...`; every endpoint there needs the `SUPPORT` or `ADMIN` role (403 otherwise, 401 without a token).

**Who can open which ticket (PARI-93).** `POST /api/tickets` is for the driver or the owner of the reservation only (404 for anyone else, also SUPPORT and ADMIN). `VEHICLE_NOT_LEFT`: owner only, from the reserved end (409 `TICKET_TOO_EARLY`), while the reservation is `IN_PROGRESS` **or `COMPLETED`** (an ended session, also an automatic check-out), otherwise 409 `SESSION_NOT_RUNNING`; one open ticket per reservation (409 `TICKET_ALREADY_OPEN`). `CANNOT_LEAVE`: driver only, only while `IN_PROGRESS`. `OTHER`: either participant, any status. The full rules, the evacuation, penalty and moderation behaviour, and the open decisions are in [support-workflows.md](support-workflows.md).

| Endpoint | What it does |
|---|---|
| `GET /api/support/tickets` | The shared queue: high priority first, then the oldest. Filters: `status`, `type`, `priority`, `unassigned`, `page`, `size`. |
| `GET /api/support/tickets/staff` | Active support agents and administrators who can be assigned a ticket (id, display name, roles). |
| `GET /api/support/tickets/{id}/reservation` | The ticket's reservation for the support page: spot and address, interval with time zone, vehicle plate, driver and owner (account ids, names, e-mail, phone), check-in and check-out, amounts, penalty, payments and refund state. Never the PIN or the QR token. 404 for an unknown ticket. |
| `GET /api/support/tickets/{id}/audit` | The audit timeline of the ticket, oldest first, paginated (`page`, `size`, default 50, at most 200). Entries: `action`, `actorId`, `actorName`, `createdAt`, `reason`, `outcome`, `metadata`. |
| `POST /api/support/tickets/{id}/claim` | Takes the ticket from the queue (409 `TICKET_ALREADY_CLAIMED` when another agent has it). |
| `POST /api/support/tickets/{id}/commands/refund-overstay-penalty` | Refunds a charged automatic overstay penalty in full (PARI-100). Body: `reason`, `operationId` (1 to 100 characters, idempotency key). Returns the `TicketView` with `overstayPenalty` (`amount`, `currency`, `state` `NONE`/`PENDING`/`CHARGED`/`FAILED`/`WAIVED`/`REFUNDED`, `refundedAmount`, `refundedAt`, `netAmount`). SUPPORT or ADMIN. 409 `OVERSTAY_PENALTY_NOT_CHARGED` (`details.state`), 409 `OVERSTAY_PENALTY_ALREADY_REFUNDED`, 402 `PAYMENT_FAILED`, 400 `VALIDATION_FAILED`. |
| `POST /api/support/tickets/{id}/commands/...` | `force-check-out`, `settle-penalty`, `cancel-with-refund`, `correct-no-show`, `sanction`, `reassign`, `release` (back to the unassigned queue, the ticket stays open), `close`. Every command needs a `reason`; a command on a closed ticket answers 409 `TICKET_CLOSED`. |
| `POST /api/support/tickets/{id}/evacuation` (and `/status`, `/fee`) | Records an evacuation: destination, status `REQUESTED` to `IN_PROGRESS` to `DONE`, fee. `/fee` sets the fee planned for this evacuation and only works before `DONE` (409 afterwards: refund the charged fee and add a new one). When the status becomes `DONE` the planned fee is charged once as an itemized evacuation fee. |
| `POST /api/support/tickets/{id}/penalties` | Assesses a penalty (PARI-87). Body: `amountMinor` (> 0, PLN minor units), `reason`, `operationId` (1 to 100 characters), optional `targetUserId` (only the reservation's driver, else 400 `PENALTY_TARGET_NOT_PAYER`). Creates a `PENDING` penalty and collects nothing. 409 `PENALTY_RESERVATION_NOT_ELIGIBLE` unless the reservation is `IN_PROGRESS`, `COMPLETED` or `NO_SHOW`. The same `operationId` again returns the ticket unchanged. |
| `POST /api/support/tickets/{id}/penalties/{penaltyId}/charge` | Collects a `PENDING` penalty from the driver's default payment method now: `CHARGED`, or `FAILED` when the payment is refused (the failed payment is stored). 409 when it is not `PENDING`. Body: `reason`. |
| `POST /api/support/tickets/{id}/penalties/{penaltyId}/waive` | Waives a `PENDING` penalty (`WAIVED`). 409 once it is charged, failed or already waived. Body: `reason`. |
| `POST /api/support/tickets/{id}/evacuation/fees` | Adds one more evacuation fee and charges it at once (PARI-88). Body: `amountMinor` (> 0), `reason`, `operationId`. Needs an evacuation on the ticket. A refused payment is stored as a `FAILED` item. The same `operationId` again changes nothing. |
| `POST /api/support/tickets/{id}/evacuation/fees/{feeId}/refund` | Reverses one charged fee in full by adding a `REFUND` item; the fee stays. 409 `EVACUATION_FEE_ALREADY_REFUNDED` on a second refund; a `FAILED` fee has nothing to refund. Body: `reason`. |
| `GET /api/support/users/{userId}/moderation` | Whether the account is blocked, the warnings that count now, the warning limit and the whole sanction history (newest first). |
| `GET /api/support/users/blocked` | Accounts that are blocked now, with the block reason and the time of the block. |
| `POST /api/support/users/{userId}/unblock` | Unblocks an account without a ticket (`reason` required, 409 `NOT_BLOCKED` when it is not blocked). The earlier sanctions stay in the history. |

**Penalties assessed by support (PARI-87).** These are separate from the automatic overstay penalty on the reservation (`overstayPenalty`, `penaltyPending`, decided with `settle-penalty`), which is unchanged. An assessed penalty has a lifecycle `PENDING` to `CHARGED`, `WAIVED` or `FAILED`; only `PENDING` can still change. Assessing records an amount and does not collect it: collection is the separate `charge` command, and the driver is charged at most once because a penalty leaves `PENDING` exactly once and its payment reference is derived from the penalty id. `FAILED` is final; to try again, assess a new penalty. The amount is PLN and has no upper limit: no maximum is defined by the project yet, so none is enforced. A penalty does not change `finalCost`, the parking price or the owner's payout. A ticket cannot be closed while a penalty assessed on it is `PENDING` (409 `PENALTY_PENDING`). `TicketView` and the reservation context list the penalties (`id`, `ticketId`, `targetUserId`, `amount`, `currency`, `reason`, `state`, `createdAt`, `decidedAt`, `decisionReason`) and `penaltyTotal`, the sum of the `CHARGED` ones.

**Evacuation fees (PARI-88).** Every evacuation charge is its own item in `evacuationFees` (`id`, `ticketId`, `kind` `FEE` or `REFUND`, `status` `CHARGED`, `FAILED` or `REFUNDED`, `amount`, `currency`, `reason`, `refundsFeeId`, `createdAt`) and is never edited. `evacuationFeeTotal` is the sum of the `CHARGED` fees minus the `REFUND` items; failed fees do not count. A correction is explicit: refund the wrong fee, then add the right one. Refunds are always for the full fee. Evacuation fees are paid as `EVAC_FEE` payments and refunds as `REFUND` payments, so they are not mixed into `PENALTY` payments, and they never change the parking price. `TicketView.evacuationFee` is only the fee planned for that ticket's evacuation. The driver's own reservation views do not show these totals yet.

**Audit policy.** Every successful support command writes one append-only entry (actor, reason, time, `outcome` `SUCCEEDED`, and safe metadata such as the previous assignee or the ticket state after the command). A command that fails rolls back and leaves no entry, so a failed command never looks like a state change. The audit entries are separate from the ticket messages and internal notes.

**Sanctions.** A sanction issued from a ticket must target the driver, the owner or the reporter of the ticket's reservation (400 `SANCTION_TARGET_NOT_PARTICIPANT` otherwise). Escalation: warnings count until the account is unblocked; when they reach the `warning_limit` platform setting (3 in the migration, a PLACEHOLDER the team may change) the account is blocked automatically and a `BLOCK` entry "Warning limit reached" is written. An unblock is a new `UNBLOCK` entry, earlier sanctions are never deleted, and the count starts again from zero. Blocking a blocked account (`ALREADY_BLOCKED`) or unblocking an active one (`NOT_BLOCKED`) answers 409.

Two requests that change the same row at once: the second answers 409 `CONCURRENT_UPDATE`; reload and try again.

### Errors

Every error has the same body, also for the security filters:

```json
{ "errorCode": "SPOT_ALREADY_RESERVED", "message": "The selected time is already reserved", "statusCode": 409, "timestamp": "2026-11-03T10:15:30Z" }
```

Some business errors add a `details` object with machine-readable facts (it is absent otherwise), for example `{ "errorCode": "CHECK_IN_TOO_EARLY", ..., "details": { "availableAt": "2026-11-06T12:55:00Z" } }`.

| Status | `errorCode` | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 400 | `VALIDATION_FAILED` | body validation failed; `message` lists `field reason` pairs |
| 400 | `BAD_REQUEST` | unreadable body, wrong parameter type, a rule such as "radius must be between 1 and 50000 meters" |
| 400 | `INVALID_CURRENT_PASSWORD` | wrong current password in change-password |
| 401 | `UNAUTHENTICATED` | no or invalid token |
| 401 | `INVALID_CREDENTIALS` | wrong e-mail or password at login (the same answer for an unknown e-mail) |
| 402 | `PAYMENT_FAILED` | the payment gateway refused (card declined, insufficient funds, refund failure) |
| 403 | `FORBIDDEN` | role or ownership rule |
| 404 | `NOT_FOUND` | unknown id, or a resource the caller may not see |
| 409 | `INVALID_STATE` | the action is not possible in the current status of the object |
| 409 | business codes | `SPOT_ALREADY_RESERVED`, `SPOT_NOT_AVAILABLE`, `SPOT_NOT_BOOKABLE`, `INSUFFICIENT_BALANCE`, `ALREADY_REVIEWED`, ... (see the table above) |
| 409 | `CONSTRAINT_VIOLATION` | safety net: a database constraint rejected the write (for example two concurrent bookings of one slot) |
| 413 | `FILE_TOO_LARGE` | upload above 5 MB |

A booking whose payment is declined answers `402`, and the reservation is stored as `CANCELLED` with the reason, so the slot is free again.

### Conventions

- **Time**: ISO-8601 instants in UTC (`2026-11-03T10:00:00Z`). Weekly availability and the owner analytics use the business time zone `Europe/Warsaw` (`pari.time-zone`).
- **Money**: the API uses decimal amounts in PLN with two decimals (`12.50`); the database stores whole grosze (`hourly_price_minor = 1250`). The conversion is done only at the edge (`Money`).
- **Prices are calculated on the server**: the client sends the space, the time and the payment-method token, never an amount. `POST /api/reservations/quote` previews the price (also public) and booking recalculates it.
- **Paging**: `page` (from 0) and `size` (default 20, at most 50) on lists; list endpoints answer with a plain JSON array.
- **Map search** (`GET /api/spots`): `lat`, `lng` are required, `radiusMeters` defaults to 5000 and is at most 50000, optional `maxPrice`, `onlyVerified`, `start` + `end` (both or none). Premium owners come first, then by distance. Without `lat` and `lng` the answer is `400`.
- **Rental types**: `bookingType` is `HOURLY` (start and end), `DAILY` (whole days) or `MONTHLY` (start and `durationMonths`, 1 to 36, with a discount from 3 months on).
- **Uploads**: `multipart/form-data`, field `file` (and `category` for `POST /api/media/upload`), JPEG, PNG or WebP (the type is detected from the bytes, not from the name), at most 5 MB. The answer holds the public URL `<PARI_PUBLIC_BASE_URL>/media/<key>`.
- **Live occupancy** (`GET /api/spots/events`): Server-Sent Events. The event name is `occupancy` and the data is `{ "spotId": "...", "occupancy": "FREE" | "OCCUPIED", "at": "...", "unitId": "...", "unitLabel": "#2", "occupiedUnits": 1, "totalUnits": 2 }` (`occupancy` is the state of the whole listing; the unit fields name the space that changed). A client must listen with `addEventListener("occupancy", ...)`; `onmessage` does not receive named events.
- **Aliases**: `GET /api/owner/payouts/history` is also served as `/withdrawals`; blocked periods as `/api/spots/{id}/blocked-periods` and `/api/spots/{id}/calendar/blocks`.

### Not implemented yet

Refresh tokens and logout on the server, e-mail and phone verification, password reset, the inspection workflow for verification requests, extending a reservation (`/extend`), the PDF confirmation, real Stripe payments, rate limiting of login. The tables for some of these already exist (see [data-dictionary.md](data-dictionary.md)).
